html:
The Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi is a huge domed shrine in the city of Turkistan in southern Kazakhstan. Timur ordered it built from 1389, over the grave of a much loved Sufi poet, and work stopped when Timur died in 1405.

Ahmed Yasawi had lived in the 12th century, as told under Ahmad Yasawi dies. He wrote wisdom poems in a Turkic language rather than Persian or Arabic, and helped spread Islam among the Turkic nomads of the steppe. His tomb had long been a place of pilgrimage. Timur built the new shrine to win the loyalty of the region's people and to show his own power.

The building is enormous, with the largest surviving brick dome in Central Asia. Its builders tried out designs later used in Timur's capital at Samarkand, such as at the Gur-e-Amir. The main entrance was never finished, and the bare brick and holes for scaffolding still show.

Later khans of the Kazakh Khanate were buried around it. In 2003 it became Kazakhstan's first UNESCO World Heritage Site.
